rule: Each 3x3 glyph (solid, X or diamond) sits at one end of a colour-8 wire. Colour-5 cells are decorations on the wire. Colour-9 blocks hide wiring, and a wire leaves a block straight through when it can. Trace each glyph's wire to its far end; the glyph centre there is two cells past the last wire cell. If a marker already sits there, nothing changes. Otherwise: a solid source becomes a diamond and an X of its colour is drawn at the far end; an X source gets a diamond at the far end; a diamond source gets an X at the far end.
scope: Construct source/target glyphs connected by crossing, turning, partially occluded wires; infer far endpoint and create the complementary marker. Latent wire routes supply outputs, while strict input tracing rejects ambiguity. Four-block controls now match the canonical test regime.

authored_scope: Random scenes have 2..6 wires between two facing glyph rows, before a random dihedral transform. Routes are straight, Z or four-turn jog, so grid sides range from about 9 to 30. Colours come from 1,2,3,4,6,7, including 7 as a synthetic extension. Source kinds S/X/D can sit on either side, and X/D connected distractors are included. Up to three 9 blocks can hide straight runs, crossings, turns and U detours. They also produce wires beside blocks, turns just outside blocks and odd port counts, each accepted only when strict tracing stays unique. Decorations flank crossings. Default scenes are hard: on some side, two or more dangling far ends are fed by out-of-order sources. Explicit single-dangling configs are accepted only as broader controls. The original fixtures use free-form routes, glyphs on perpendicular sides and long multi-turn wires. They are rebuilt through explicit latent arguments (width, height, wires, blocks, decorations), with outputs derived from the declared connections. Random scenes never have glyphs on perpendicular sides, routes with more than four turns, wires beside glyphs, or decorations away from crossings. The public input_grid solver path has been removed.
authored_constraints: All grid sides are in 1..30, and marker colours are distinct values from {1,2,3,4,6,7}.
Wires meet only at clean perpendicular crossings. A crossing is never an end or corner of either wire, and a wire never overlaps itself.
Glyph slots, filled or empty, lie in bounds, contain no wire, 9 or 5 cells, and have centres at Chebyshev distance >= 4 from each other.
9 blocks are rectangles that do not touch (random scenes keep a 2-cell gap). Each hides at least one wire cell, and none hides a wire end or a glyph slot.
Decorations sit only on plain, visible, single-occupancy wire cells (not ends, corners or crossings).

Every glyph traces to its latent partner slot under the strict rule: one start direction, one turn candidate, and a unique straight block exit or a single exit. Otherwise the scene is rejected or raises ValueError.
At least one wire is single-source, so no sample is identity-only.

In default random scenes, some side has >= 2 dangling far ends whose single-source wires form an inversion (source order differs from far-end order). This rules out the straight-across and rank-order shortcuts.
Outputs are stamped from the latent wire endpoints and kinds, never by parsing the rendered grid.
